subject: Eval sign-off criteria for FP8/INT8 defaults (hosted catalog)
body:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Arjun Desai <arjun.desai@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Henry Cho <henry.cho@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 11, 2026 at 9:12 AM
Subject: Eval sign-off criteria for FP8/INT8 defaults (hosted catalog)
Attachments: FP8_INT8_Default_Enablement_Signoff_Checklist_v0.3.docx; Quality_Sanity_Suite_Results_Template_v1.xlsx

Arjun + Henry,

We need a crisp set of sign-off criteria for when we can flip FP8/INT8 as the DEFAULT for a hosted model variant (vs. opt-in behind a flag). This is blocking PM-1185 and also what we tell Product re: “recommended by default”.

Proposal for “default enablement” gate (please poke holes):

A) Correctness / safety gates (must pass)
- Kernel correctness: CI smoke bench for quantized correctness passes on representative shape set (prefill + decode) for the target GPU(s).
- Numerical sanity: no NaNs/inf; output tokenization stable; deterministic seed drift within expected bounds.
- Runtime regressions: no increase in error rate > +0.05% absolute during canary (by model/GPU/region).

B) Quality gates (must pass on Top Hosted Models Benchmark Suite v3)
Run suite on:
- “General chat” distribution (short/medium prompts)
- “Long-context” distribution (>= 8k context bucket)
- Tool-calling / structured-output variants (JSON schema + function call)
- Safety/refusal set (to ensure we didn’t weaken refusal behavior)

Thresholds (initial strawman):
- Aggregate quality score delta: <= 0.3% relative drop vs baseline (FP16/BF16) on each of the 4 categories above.
- No single prompt set bucket with > 1.0% relative drop.
- Human spot-check: 20 samples on the long-context set for the top 2 customer-like tasks per model family (summarization + extraction) with “no obvious degradation”.

C) Performance gates (canary + benchmark)
- End-to-end: TTFT p50 must not regress > 2%; p95 must not regress > 3% for the suite distributions. (We can allow TTFT regressions if TPOT/tokens/s improves enough? TBD.)
- Throughput: tokens/s improvement must be >= 5% on at least 2 workload profiles (prefill-heavy and decode-heavy) for the target fleet GPU.
- Variance: coefficient of variation within benchmarking standards.

D) Eligibility rules
- FP8 default only on H100 initially; A100 and cost SKUs (L4) require separate sign-off.
- INT8 default: only if calibration requirements met (need your take Arjun) + no known quality cliffs for long context.

Could you respond with:
1) Anything we should tighten/loosen, especially around INT8 calibration requirements.
2) What you want as “required prompt sets” (naming + where they live) so this doesn’t drift.
3) Henry: what language you need for “perf transparency” / what we can claim vs must footnote.

If we agree today, I’ll turn it into the policy page + checklist that’s referenced from the sprint plan.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
Performance & Evals
Redwood Inference

From: Arjun Desai <arjun.desai@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Henry Cho <henry.cho@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 11, 2026 at 10:01 AM
Subject: Re: Eval sign-off criteria for FP8/INT8 defaults (hosted catalog)

This is directionally right.

INT8-specific notes (where we’ve gotten burned):

1) Calibration is non-negotiable for default INT8.
- Require per-model-family calibration artifacts (activation ranges) produced from a fixed calibration set + fixed seed.
- If we ship INT8 without calibrated ranges we’ll see “looks fine on short prompts, falls over on extraction + long context”.

2) Add a “schema adherence” metric for structured output.
- We should score JSON validity rate and “field presence” rate, not just an aggregate quality scalar.
- INT8 can keep the semantics but start dropping keys or hallucinating wrong types.

3) Long-context should be mandatory for FP8 too.
- We’ve seen mild regression on 16k+ buckets in one model family; it was invisible in short prompt distributions.

4) Default enablement should be GPU-scoped.
- Agree: FP8 default for H100 only.
- INT8 default for A100 is likely OK for matmul-heavy models, but we should treat it as “opt-in” until we have a clean playbook + customer guardrails.

Prompt sets: I’d reference the Suite v3 doc (Confluence) as the source of truth + pin to a version/hash (so it’s reproducible). Also strongly recommend we include:
- “Summarization (enterprise-style)”: the set we use in the sales deep dives.
- “RAG extraction”: multi-field extraction with exact-match checks.

Also: for INT8, please add a hard rule: if any bucket shows > 0.5% absolute increase in “unparseable JSON” or tool-call failures, we do NOT default-enable.

— Arjun
Arjun Desai
Quantization Profiles
Redwood Inference

From: Henry Cho <henry.cho@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Arjun Desai <arjun.desai@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 11, 2026 at 11:34 AM
Subject: Re: Eval sign-off criteria for FP8/INT8 defaults (hosted catalog)

+1 to Arjun’s points.

On perf transparency / what we can claim:
- We need a clear rule for “default enabled” vs “available” vs “experimental”, because the public-facing bench copy and internal sales enablement differ.
- We should only claim “X% faster” on charts if:
  (a) methodology is pinned (suite version, hardware SKU, driver/CUDA, batch/concurrency),
  (b) results are reproducible (variance within standards),
  (c) and the model variant is actually the default in Hosted (not just behind a flag for a week).

Questions for you:
1) Are we OK with different thresholds for TTFT vs TPOT? (TTFT can regress slightly if decode dominates for customer value, but we need guardrails.)
2) Do we need an explicit “no customer-impact rollback events in canary for N days” before we call something the new default? Even if quality/perf looks fine in the lab.

If you can include a short “approved claim template” (1-2 bullets + required footnotes) that would unblock PM-1184 too.

— Henry
Henry Cho
Product, Performance Transparency
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Henry Cho <henry.cho@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Arjun Desai <arjun.desai@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 11, 2026 at 1:06 PM
Subject: Re: Eval sign-off criteria for FP8/INT8 defaults (hosted catalog)

Good callouts.

Re (1) TTFT vs TPOT thresholds:
- I’d rather make it explicit by workload class:
  - For interactive/chat workloads (short prompts, low concurrency), TTFT is a primary SLO.
  - For batch summarization / extraction (long prompts, higher concurrency), TPOT/tokens/s dominates.

Proposed gate wording:
- “No net SLO regression”:
  - Interactive profile: TTFT p50 <= +2%, TTFT p95 <= +3%.
  - Batch profile: TPOT p50 <= +2% AND tokens/s >= +5%.
- If interactive regresses but batch improves, default-enable only for workloads/tiers where the scheduler routes to batch profile (i.e., NOT global default). That implies product needs a concept of “default by tier/pool”, which we don’t have cleanly yet.

Re (2) “N days of clean canary”:
- Yes. Add a “stability gate”: 48 hours in perf canary with:
  - no auto-rollback,
  - no p95 TTFT breaches beyond thresholds,
  - error rate delta <= +0.05% abs,
  - and sample size >= X requests (we should align with ENG-7426 noise handling).

Approved claim template (internal + external-ish):
- Claim: “For Model X on H100, Redwood’s FP8 default improves throughput by Y% (tokens/s) vs BF16 on the Top Hosted Models Benchmark Suite v3.”
- Required footnotes:
  - Suite v3 (commit/hash), prompt-length distribution, prefill/decode mix.
  - Hardware SKU + driver/CUDA/container version.
  - Batch size / concurrency settings.
  - “Quality checked: no material regression on Suite v3 categories; structured output validity unchanged.”

Arjun: I’ll incorporate JSON/tool-call validity as a hard gate (absolute delta) for INT8 and likely FP8 too.

— Jonas

From: Arjun Desai <arjun.desai@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Henry Cho <henry.cho@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 11, 2026 at 2:22 PM
Subject: Re: Eval sign-off criteria for FP8/INT8 defaults (hosted catalog)

One more nuance: “model family exceptions”.

We should explicitly allow a per-model override with a clear reason:
- Example: Model M (long-context) has a known FP8 quality cliff beyond 12k unless we use a different quant profile. In that case FP8 can be default only for <= 8k contexts (or only for certain regions/SKUs), otherwise “available but not default”.

So add to the policy:
- Any default enablement must declare:
  - max context length supported under the default quant mode,
  - and whether tool-calling / structured output is supported in default.

Also suggest we add a “regression quarantine” rule:
- If canary catches a rollback (even if it’s a harness flake), default enablement is paused until we have a written root cause + mitigation. Prevents whiplash.

— Arjun

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Arjun Desai <arjun.desai@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Henry Cho <henry.cho@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 11, 2026 at 4:48 PM
Subject: Re: Eval sign-off criteria for FP8/INT8 defaults (hosted catalog)

Locking this in as v1 (I’ll publish to Confluence tonight and link from PM-1185).

Summary — “Default enablement” sign-off criteria for FP8/INT8 hosted variants:

1) Required eval suite (pinned)
- Top Hosted Models Benchmark Suite v3 (pinned version/hash)
  - General chat distribution
  - Long-context distribution
  - Tool-calling + structured output (JSON schema)
  - Safety/refusal set
- Plus model-family add-ons as needed (Summarization enterprise-style; RAG extraction exact-match)

2) Hard quality gates
- Aggregate quality delta <= 0.3% relative drop per category.
- No bucket > 1.0% relative drop.
- Structured output validity: unparseable JSON/tool-call failures must not increase > 0.5% absolute.
- Human spot-check (20 samples) for long-context summarization + extraction: “no obvious degradation”.

3) INT8 calibration requirements
- Required: published calibration artifacts for the model family (activation ranges) generated from fixed calibration set + fixed seed.
- No “uncalibrated INT8” can be default-enabled.

4) Perf + stability gates
- Interactive profile: TTFT p50 <= +2% and p95 <= +3% vs baseline.
- Batch profile: TPOT p50 <= +2% and tokens/s >= +5% vs baseline.
- Canary stability: 48h, no auto-rollback, error rate delta <= +0.05% abs, min sample size per ENG-7426.
- Any canary rollback pauses default enablement until RCA + mitigation is written.

5) Scope + explicit declarations
- Default enablement is GPU-scoped (FP8 default: H100-only for now).
- Any default must declare max context length for that quant mode + whether structured output/tool-calling is supported.
- Model-family exception allowed only with written reason + explicit constraint (e.g., FP8 default <= 8k ctx).

Henry: I’ll add the “approved claim template + required footnotes” section you asked for.
Arjun: please send me the exact calibration set identifier you want referenced (name + where it lives) so we don’t keep reinventing it.

Thanks both.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber

Redwood Inference
